P1.evidence: Setter information was read back twice and used well: 'I've already heard a few things from him, of course, from the chats that you've had already together' and later 'I already heard from Trevor as well, that you have some things with your mobility at the moment, but I think it's something in your lower back that sometimes freezes.' No frame was set at all — the rep went straight from rapport to 'let's just dive into it' — and no frame agreement was sought. Open question asked: 'can you take me through like what we can potentially help you with?'

P2.evidence: Work, training week, diet and energy were all asked properly. 'what do you actually do for work that it's stressful?' established art dealing and working from home. 'what's your energy like at the moment?' produced a rich answer about the 1.30pm cutoff. Nutrition was probed to frequency ('is it like a daily thing... or is it like a weekly thing?'). But age, height and weight were never asked (58 was volunteered), health conditions were never asked, the back injury was raised from setter notes rather than asked open and never followed up for duration or clinical history, results were never asked, and sleep was never asked.

P3.evidence: The bridge question was asked and asked well: 'You're 58. I can already say you don't look 58... you're already in good shape... Why do you want to achieve the better shape? Like, you're already in a good state, right?' The answer that came back was surface — 'you're never happy what you've got, you always want to have better' — and the rep did not push once. He never asked what better movement would do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove to family, identity or longevity. On a 58-year-old with a recurring back injury there was a longevity driver available and it was left untouched. This is why $6,000 landed against nothing.

P4.evidence: Entirely skipped. The prospect volunteered a prior online trainer in LA, a Pilates habit he dropped, and an abandoned kettlebell attempt after injuring his back — three complete past-attempt stories — and not one was asked about, followed up or converted into a root cause.

P5.evidence: Entirely skipped. No question about what happens if nothing changes, no willingness-to-settle test, no line in the sand. The prospect went on to say 'it's less of a transformation... I see it as an additional bonus' — the exact belief Phase 5 exists to move — and the rep agreed with him: 'It comes down to getting from good to best, right?'

P6.evidence: 'Anything else that you feel like that, that's what I would need from Trevor?' is a weak variant of P6b and got a flat 'No, I think that's it.' Later 'outside of timing wise, you feel like, yeah, I do want to do this' obtained a yes about scheduling only. No genuine commitment was secured before presenting — the prospect said 'I don't even know how does it function, what it costs' at the point the presentation ended.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The rep never asked for the business, never sent a link and ended on 'have think about it'.

objection_plays.detail: Textbook trigger, twice: 'Well, I would have to think about it' and 'you have to just let me think then, before I go anywhere further.' Not one scripted move ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep replied 'Sounds good. I would say, have think about it.'

Trigger present in two forms — 'That's a lot of money' and 'my cash flow is not great, because there's a lot of open invoices that have not been paid'. Finances were never isolated, no financial-picture question was asked, no plan was offered. Instead of running the play the rep discounted the anchor himself by volunteering a $4,000-$6,000 range.

Trigger present: 'this is my last week and I don't think I have time because I had to pack everything... I'll be too distracted to start with something new this week.' The rep ran one probe — 'What makes you be like, why not now?' — then accommodated with a 24 July start date. None of the scripted moves ran: no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up'.

Fear of harm was explicit: 'I can't do kettlebells anymore, it's too dangerous and stuff' and 'I don't want to do movements that provoke a lower back pain.' No certainty question, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before. The rep offered only a form-correction promise.

Two script gaps fired on this call. First, a cheaper alternative that genuinely works: an in-person trainer at 75 pounds an hour and a prior online coach at roughly $500 for three months. Second, a clinical fit objection — the exact movement being sold (snatches) is what injured his back. Neither has a scripted path and the rep improvised a partial-value reframe on the first ('It's about the same') and a reassurance on the second.

notes: Phase 2 was the strongest work on this call and Phases 4 and 5 were skipped entirely, which is the whole story: the rep built a factual picture, never built a reason, then presented into a vacuum. The single highest-leverage correction is to hold the price — resistance was answered within seconds by volunteering a lower range, which taught the prospect the number was negotiable and removed any reason to decide today.
